title: Settlement Basis: Tax and Carrier Fee Return on Air Ticket Fare Brands
content:
**Air Ticket Fare Brands — settlement basis for the tax and carrier fee return.**

The taxes and carrier fees the airline returns on a booking the traveller has given up are taken as the total of the tax lines posted on the booking, returned in full to the original form of payment.

**The stage settled first.** The amount the tax lines are returned at is settled first, and the amount returned is that figure with anything held back taken off it and anything else that comes back added to it, each share and each uplift that bears on the figure acting in turn on the figure the one before it gives, so that the figure runs on from one step to the next and is never reached by measuring them separately against the figure as it was settled and netting the results together. The amount held back is that share of the amount the tax lines are returned at, the figure settled at the first stage, taken on that figure as it stands when the share falls to be taken; anything else that comes back is added in dollars to that figure as it then stands.

**Shares and uplifts on one figure.** Where more than one share is taken on the same figure, the shares act one after another, each on the figure the one before it gives, and are never combined into a single rate; where more than one uplift is added to the same figure, the uplifts are combined into a single uplift and the figure is increased once by that total.

**Against which line the amount is raised.** The amount returned is settled as one payout line raised against the tax line posted earliest on the booking. That payout line carries the traveller position of the tax line it is raised against.

**The money collected.** The money collected on the booking is the total of its fare, tax and service lines — the service line being the agency service fee of the fare brand held — together with its optional extras, its rework lines and its penalty lines. It never includes the travel credit the booking has issued or redeemed. The amount returned may never exceed the money collected on the booking.

**Rounding.** The amount returned is rounded to two decimal places at the end and never at any intermediate step.

**A determination on hypothetical figures.** Every figure and every rate in what follows is hypothetical, chosen only to show the whole chain being carried, and no rate below is a published one. Take a booking carrying two tax lines of 84.20 and 41.55 US dollars, the earlier of them posted for the first traveller, a fare line of 612.00, a service line of 24.95, one optional extra at 35.00 and a rework line at 75.00, with no penalty line and no travel credit issued or redeemed. The tax lines total 125.75, so the amount the tax lines are returned at is settled at 125.75, and the amount returned follows from that settled figure. Suppose a share of 0.88 bears on it, so that the part held back is what that share leaves off: 125.75 taken at 0.88 gives 110.66. Suppose an uplift of 0.42 then bears on the figure that share gave: 110.66 increased by 0.42 gives 157.1372. Suppose 12.00 US dollars then comes back in dollars, landing on the figure the uplift gave: 157.1372 with 12.00 added gives 169.1372. Each step is worked on the figure the step before it gave, and no step is worked on the 125.75 the stage settled at; nothing is rounded along the way. The money collected on the booking is 612.00, 125.75, 24.95, 35.00 and 75.00 totalled, which is 872.70, and 169.1372 does not exceed it, so that ceiling does not bite. Rounded to two decimal places at the end, 169.14 US dollars goes back to the original form of payment, as one payout line raised against the tax line posted earliest and carrying the first traveller position.
